title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1966-09-16
source: SBD>MR>?>LP>ZoomH4>WaveLab 5.0>FLAC24</br>Linn LP12 turntable, SME III tonearm, Benz ACE H2 Cartridge, Rotel RC 1082 preamp</br>Transfer by indidarkstar

ai_review.summary: Clean, well‑balanced vinyl rip captures a high‑energy early‑Dead show with scorching “I Know You Rider”, “Dancing in the Streets” and “Baby Blue”.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its low surface noise, clear separation and faithful pitch – essentially a very clean transfer of the original Avalon LPs. Musically the performance shines: Jerry’s lightning‑fast solos, tight drum/guitar interplay and enthusiastic crowd make this an early‑Dead highlight, especially on “I Know You Rider”, “Dancing in the Streets” and “All Over Now, Baby Blue”.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and extol both the musical excitement and the clean vinyl source; recording quality is consistently described as good to excellent.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean vinyl rip with very little surface noise, slightly lower levels and wider channel separation than other versions; balanced mix that matches original pitch, occasional low‑level quirks but overall clear and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑era set that feels loose and playful; the band is clearly feeding off each other's energy, with a strong early‑show drive that builds into extended solos and tight group improvisation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for blistering, jazz‑inflected solo work and high‑speed bluegrass/acid runs; considered one of his finest early performances.
band_member_comments.Drums: Interplay between drums and lead guitar highlighted as a “question and answer” dynamic that lifts the whole performance.
